content: Breast shells are hollow plastic discs designed to be worn inside a brassiere to prevent the nipple from becoming flattened. These discs feature a central hole that is positioned toward the nipple side. The structure of the shell is slightly concave to conform to the natural shape of the breast, although they may still be slightly visible under tight clothing. Breast shells are designed to be taken apart for cleaning, which should be done frequently. This is because the shell can cause the breast to sweat, creating an environment conducive to bacterial growth and potential irritation. These devices are often used to protect engorged or sore nipples during breastfeeding. Additionally, breast shells can help encourage an inverted nipple to protrude. If the shell is being used to prepare the mother for breastfeeding, it is most effective when used during pregnancy. However, it is important to note that the use of breast shells can increase the leakage of breast milk or colostrum. Some research indicates that using breast shells on inverted nipples may actually interfere with the mother’s ability to breastfeed successfully. Breast shells can also be used to collect milk when the baby has not finished nursing from the breast. It is important to distinguish breast shells from nipple shields. Nipple shields are specifically designed for use during the act of breastfeeding, whereas breast shells are intended for use in preparation for or after breastfeeding.
